summary: The study describes the fabrication of a HfO2/HfOxNy/HfO2 gate dielectric using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) with H2 plasma as a reactant and tetrakis(dimethylamino)hafnium as a precursor. The incorporation of nitrogen into the gate oxide reduces capacitance equivalent oxide thickness (CET), interface trap density (Dit), trapped positive charge density (ΔNp), and gate leakage currents while maintaining comparable hysteresis. The results are attributed to the presence of N–H bonds, which reduce localized states and prevent conduction-band lowering, and the decrement of N–N and N–O bonds, which contribute to trap density.
evidence: By using H2 plasma as a reactant with tetrakis(dimethylamino)hafnium precursor during plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition, we deposited the HfOxNy layer between HfO2 layers. The 5 nm thick HfO2/HfOxNy/HfO2/HfONO trilayer gate oxide shows reduced capacitance equivalent oxide thickness (CET) than that of the HfO2 film with the same thickness due to the contribution of nitrogen incorporation to the high dielectric constant. The HfONO film utilizing H2 plasma shows lower values of interface trap density (Dit), trapped positive charge density (ΔNp), and gate leakage currents than the HfO2 layer with the same thickness while maintaining comparable hysteresis. The results can be attributed to the presence of N–H bonds, which can reduce localized states below the conduction band and prevent the conduction-band lowering, and decrement of N–N and N–O bonds, which contribute to trap density, confirmed by the combination of X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and near-edge X-ray absorption fine-structure analyses.
